messages:
samir: Customer report: intermittent Invalid JSON errors from JSON mode streaming responses. Happens only when requests go through our customer's internal proxy + nginx. Error: 'Unexpected end of JSON input' on client side.

ashley-support: thanks, can you paste a minimal trace / logs from the SDK and the raw wire chunks if available?

samir: pasted from user's Node app (ts-sdk v0.9.3) — they collect raw chunks and concat then JSON.parse -> sometimes fails. Logged chunk frames: 
```
3e\n{\"id\":\"r1\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"text\":\"Hello\"}}]}\n\n0\n\n
```
then in failing case: 
```
1f\n{\"id\":\"r1\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"text\":\"Hello\"}}]}\n\n0\n\n\r\n
```
The client sees an extra CRLF after the terminating 0 chunk which makes the concatenation include an extra "\r" byte. JSON.parse throws.

olga-eng: interesting — chunked transfer encoding should end with "0\r\n\r\n" exactly. If there's an extra "\r\n" after that we might be double-appending when proxy re-chunks. Do we have repro with our python sdk or go?

matt-qa: I ran a quick Go client against a tiny express proxy that adds keepalive and re-chunks. Repro: sometimes the last frame is split: server sends `0\r\n\r\n`, proxy forwards `0\r\n` then another packet with `\r\n`. Our streaming parser (Go json.Decoder over a Reader) chokes because it sees EOF before getting the final "\r\n" framed boundary and returns unexpected EOF. log: `json: unexpected EOF`.

kai-eng: we need to know whether this is a serializer bug (we're emitting an extra CRLF) or the proxy altering chunks. Can the customer share wget/curl raw capture? tcpdump or `ngrep -W byline` would help. Also we should check our SDKs' streaming concat logic: we currently buffer raw bytes and then call JSON.parse on the joined buffer — that will fail on stray control bytes. We should strip trailing whitespace/newlines before parse as a defensive measure.

samir: customer provided tcpdump snippet (sanitized):
```
...
485: GET /v1/responses HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.test
...
200: HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

5
{\"a\":
...
0

\r\n
```
They say their internal proxy uses chunked buffering and occasionally appends an extra CRLF.

ashley-support: workaround suggestion to the customer: if using JS/TS SDK, wrapper around streaming parser to trim trailing whitespace before JSON.parse and tolerate an extra CRLF. For Python/Go, recommend using a buffered reader that consumes trailing \r\n and retry on EOF with small backoff.

olga-eng: long-term: SDKs should be robust. I propose the following action items:
- TS SDK: when in JSON mode, after assembling final message buffer, run a small sanitize step: rtrim bytes 
- Py SDK: when using streaming mode, detect EOF and check if buffer ends with CRLF sequences, drop extra bytes then attempt json.loads again
- Go SDK: wrap io.Reader in a tolerant reader that consumes trailing CRLF before decoding

matt-qa: also add an end-to-end test with an nginx proxy configured with `proxy_buffering on; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` and a flaky re-chunker that sometimes splits the final chunk. We can simulate by inserting `sleep(0.01)` between sends.

kai-eng: note: be careful not to silently allow truncated JSON (we must only strip whitespace/newline control bytes). Add strict logging and a counter metric for sanitized JSON occurrences to monitor in prod.

samir: customer escalation: they also see an auth failure sometimes immediately after parse error in logs (401). Suspect connection reuse/keepalive causing a misaligned response to be read as part of next request. Customer uses HTTP/1.1 keepalive + proxy pooling.

olga-eng: that's concerning — if a previous response left extra bytes in the connection, the next request could read the stray \r\n as part of a new response header and break parsing. We should recommend disabling connection pooling at their proxy temporarily. Also add a server-side guard: ensure responses are flushed and then the connection is in a clean state.

ashley-support: I asked the customer to try `curl --no-keepalive` and to run a repro with `env REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1` to capture raw bytes.

dev-bot: tagging internal owners: @olga-eng @kai-eng. Escalation priority: P2.

matt-qa: I will open a small ticket with steps + a docker-compose repro (node proxy, nginx re-chunker, three clients: ts, py, go). Patch will include the sanitize step in all SDKs behind a feature flag `jsonmode_tolerant_parse=true` so we can rollout slowly.

samir: customer accepted the workaround for now. They will try disabling pooling and share tcpdump. I'm leaving the thread open until we have the sdk patches. :thumbsup:

ashley-support: thanks — please update here when the reproducible test is checked in.
